claim: Simon's thesis: ill-structured problems need no new kind of process. The same search plus memory retrieval, working on a locally well-structured sub-problem at each moment, covers them.
agent_test: Compare one scaffold on open tasks against a variant with a separate 'creative mode' at equal tokens. Expect no gain from the extra mode.

claim: Whether a task counts as ill-structured depends on the solver and its resources (Simon 1973: chess is well-structured in the small, ill-structured in the large). A mechanizable test of solutions is one of Simon's criteria for a well-structured problem, and external verifier loops lift LLM planning where a verifier exists (Kambhampati 2024); this suggests, but no opened source tests, that adding a code check makes a sub-problem more searchable.
agent_test: Run the same open task with and without an executable checker on sub-steps at equal tokens. Measure pass rate.
audit_note: Simon supports solver-relative structure and a mechanizable test as a WSP criterion, and Kambhampati shows verifier loops help, but no source shows that adding a code check turns a sub-problem well-structured and searchable; that is the researcher's inference, and Huang is about self-correction, not structure.
claim_before_audit: Whether a task is ill-structured depends on the solver and its checks. Adding a code check or tool makes a sub-problem well-structured and searchable.

claim: Explicit search with lookahead and backtracking beats single-pass chain of thought on tasks with a crisp test. Game of 24, GPT-4: CoT 4.0%, ToT b=5 74%. Crosswords: removing backtracking cut word-level success from 60% to 20%.
agent_test: Re-run Game of 24 and a held-out puzzle set with flat CoT vs the S6 tree at equal tokens.
audit_note: Only the ToT paper was opened as an independent check (other listed items are the same paper); numbers match. Other ToT-family entries not needed for the claim.

claim: At roughly equal tokens, search beats UNVERIFIED sampling of many chains: ToT used 5.5k completion tokens, close to 100 CoT trials (6.7k), and reached 74% vs 49% for best-of-100 CoT on Game of 24. But a cost-matched rerun that pairs 150 plain GPT-4 queries with a sound external verifier reaches 70%, so the edge over verified sampling is about 4 points. MCTS-style search costs dozens of times more tokens than sampling plus voting in another study.
agent_test: Equal-token test with three arms on the same items: tree search, best-of-N with an external verifier, best-of-N without one. LATS and RAP gains are not equal-budget.

claim: Early commitment is where chain-of-thought fails. About 60% of CoT samples on Game of 24 were already wrong after the first step.
agent_test: Log the step of first fatal error in baseline runs. Test branching only at step 1 vs uniform branching.

claim: Self-evaluation is a weak link in search and revision. The ToT pruning heuristic loses correct branches (crossword best-state oracle 7 of 20 games vs 4 of 20), and a model's own review without outside feedback does not help. A model verifier on Game of 24 (no chain of thought) rejected 20.7% of correct answers (213 of 1029). In tree search for web agents a stronger scorer lifted success from 28.5% to 37.0% and a ground-truth reward reached 43.5%.
agent_test: Replace the model evaluator by a code or held-out check in S6 and compare at equal tokens. Log pruned-correct branches.
audit_note: Minor: the 28.5 to 37.0 lift in Koh et al. comes from self-consistency (n=20 samples) on the same GPT-4o scorer, a stronger scoring ensemble rather than a different model.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction hurts. GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA fell 75.8 to 38.1 (3 calls) and 41.8 (5 calls); GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0. Reported gains came from oracle labels (GPT-3.5 CSQA 89.7 with oracle). Checked in the source tables.
agent_test: Run revise-without-check vs revise-with-code-feedback on the agent. Expect the second to win.

claim: External verifier loops lift planning a lot where a verifier exists. Blocksworld reached 82% within 15 back-prompts (plain GPT-4 34.3% in PlanBench, about 12% in the position paper); TravelPlanner about 6x from a 0.6% base.
agent_test: Back-prompt loop with verifier at a fixed round cap vs single-shot. Count tokens.
audit_note: Minor: the 6x TravelPlanner figure is paired with TravelPlanner's own 0.6% GPT-4-Turbo base, which is a combination of two papers.

claim: Bare LLM planning depends on recognised surface form. Pre-reasoning models score 8 to 63% on Blocksworld and 0 to 4.3% on Mystery Blocksworld (obfuscated names). o1-preview scores 97.8% on plain, 52.8% on Mystery and 37.3% on Randomized Mystery, and 23.63% on 20-40 step plans.
agent_test: Run obfuscated variants of each test item. A large gap means retrieval, not search.
audit_note: Numbers match the PlanBench o1 paper, but every listed source (Valmeekam 2023, Kambhampati 2024, Valmeekam 2024) comes from the same Kambhampati/Valmeekam ASU group, so the surface-form claim rests on one lab.

claim: Making the model write out or simulate the search helps. Searchformer solved 93.7% of unseen Sokoban with 26.8% fewer steps than A*. RAP with LLaMA-33B beat GPT-4 CoT at 2 and 4 steps (1.00 and 0.88 vs 0.50 and 0.63) but was about level at 6 steps (0.42 vs 0.40).
agent_test: Searchformer needs training, so test only the visible search record and world-model rollouts. Compare with GPT-4-class CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Fixation is real in humans. A primed group built costlier bridges (d=1.10, N=36) and kept the costly method in 83% vs 44% of participants when both worked.
agent_test: Prime the agent with a flawed example, then measure whether it repeats the flawed feature. Test a forced-alternative operator.

claim: Examples help or hurt by condition. A 43-study meta-analysis found examples cut idea variety but raise novelty and quality, best with few and uncommon examples. Effect sizes were not read.
agent_test: Vary number and commonness of examples shown to the agent. Measure variety and quality.

claim: LLMs show design fixation. ChatGPT kept iterating one concept, latched on to the last-listed item, forgot constraints and dropped a promising concept after a setback. Chair designs repeated familiar features (unique terms 67.4% vs 78.2% for human award entries).
agent_test: Count distinct concept families over N runs with and without an explicit 'name 3 different families first' step. Check that a ledger prevents forgotten constraints.
audit_note: Minor: Egea is a single qualitative hackathon case (one LLM-led team), so 'LLMs show design fixation' generalises from small samples.

claim: LLM output is less diverse than crowds at group level, and AI help narrows group diversity while raising individual quality. Doshi and Hauser: novelty +6.7%, similarity to AI ideas +5.2%. GPT-4 was below human crowds under every setting. A critique-critique second pass gave the largest diversity gain.
agent_test: Measure embedding diversity across independent runs. Test a self-critique diversity pass vs plain resampling at equal tokens.

claim: Raw temperature, top-p and min-p do not fix low diversity. Across 25 models, 50 responses per query, average pairwise similarity exceeds 0.8 in 79% of cases at top-p 0.9, T=1, and still typically exceeds 0.8 under min-p 0.1 at T=2. Prompt structure matters more.
agent_test: Sweep sampling parameters vs prompt-level diversity operators at equal tokens.

claim: Generating more hits a ceiling. Of 4000 LLM research ideas per topic, only about 200 were non-duplicates.
agent_test: Track unique-idea count against samples drawn. Stop S6 branching when the duplicate rate passes a threshold.

claim: LLM ideas were rated more novel than expert human ideas (5.64 vs 4.84; AI plus human rerank 5.81), slightly less feasible, but reviewers barely agreed (56.1% vs 50% chance). Chakrabarty found LLM stories 3 to 10 times less likely to pass creativity tests. The sources conflict on LLM creativity.
agent_test: Use blind multi-rater or code-checkable scoring. Never accept a model-graded win alone.

claim: Model-graded gains on open tasks are weak evidence. ToT creative-writing coherence (7.56 vs 6.19) was judged by GPT-4, and the human check was by the authors.
agent_test: Re-judge with a different model and with blind humans.

claim: Design problem and solution spaces co-evolve, and creative moments pair a framing with a partial solution (N=9 designers). Solution-driven designers scored lower on quality but higher on creativity. Mostly abstract-level sources.
agent_test: Allow S6 to change the problem statement as well as the candidate. Compare with solution-only search.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Simon predicts order-dependence and neglected interactions in local sub-problem design. The final design depends on step order and earlier decisions get undone. LLM hackathon evidence shows forgotten constraints.
agent_test: Run two step orders on the same brief. Measure constraint violations with and without a ledger. TravelPlanner subset: GPT-4-Turbo passes 63.3% of commonsense checks per item but only 2.0% of plans pass all of them; use that micro versus macro gap as the target.

claim: LLM help with problem reframing gave no measurable gain for human designers (N=280, four conditions, no significant novelty or usefulness difference). More competent designers got more novel frames. Users regenerated structured content repeatedly.
agent_test: Test an agent reframe operator on frame quality with blind raters. Expect no gain unless a check exists.

claim: In open engineering design with simulator feedback, iteration lifts success (o3 34.38% single-shot to almost 60% after 10 iterations), but not where the model lacks domain skill (analog IC 0% throughout). CoT gain was small (14.29% vs 12.70% pass).
agent_test: Closed-loop design with a simulator at a fixed iteration cap vs single-shot. Count tokens.

claim: Difficulty rises with ill-structuredness. EngiBench Level 1 is mostly 77 to 98% accurate while open Level 3 drops and humans beat all models. GraphicBench plans looked right but often failed in execution (VQA pass rate about 27.5 to 39.6%).
agent_test: Stratify test items by structure level. Report scaffold gain per level.
audit_note: Minor: EngiBench Level 1 is accuracy % but Level 3 is a 0-10 rubric, so the drop is across different metrics; Level 1 upper bound 98 only loosely checked in a figure-heavy PDF.

claim: An LLM can sometimes do the problem-formulation step (natural language to states, operators, goal) that a symbolic search then uses, but not reliably. Water-jug tests succeeded; on 9 classic planning domains the best model gave valid PDDL in 94% of domains but a functionally equivalent domain in only 25%.
agent_test: Test LLM-formulated problem space plus code search on tasks with verified answers. Score the formulation separately.

claim: Among the opened studies, the tree-search gains on tasks with an exact external check are large (Game of 24, crosswords, VisualWebArena +39.7% relative, WebArena +28.0%); the one open-ended test, ToT creative writing, was judged only by GPT-4 scores (7.56 vs 6.93 CoT) and a human preference comparison, and no opened study measures tree search against an expert verdict on a truly ill-structured brief.
agent_test: Pick an open task with a delayed external verdict. Compare scaffold vs plain at equal tokens.
audit_note: Numbers for Koh et al. and Brown et al. match, but the ToT paper (opened in the same batch) measured a tree-search gain on open-ended Creative Writing judged by GPT-4 scores and human pairwise preference, so 'all measured search gains are on tasks with a check' is too broad.
claim_before_audit: No opened study measures a tree search on a truly ill-structured task with an external verdict. All measured search gains are on tasks with a check. Closest new case: best-first tree search on web tasks (VisualWebArena +39.7% relative, WebArena +28.0%) is open-ended and long, but the final success check is exact. Gap 2 stays open for expert-judged briefs.

claim: No single search method is best; the right one depends on item difficulty. Beam search wins on hard maths items, plain best-of-N or sequential revision wins on easy ones, and lookahead search underperforms at equal budget. For reasoning models at matched tokens, non-thinking equals or beats thinking at low complexity, thinking wins at medium, both collapse at high.
agent_test: Add a difficulty probe before S6. Compare always-search, never-search and gated search at equal tokens across easy, medium and hard items.
audit_note: Minor: Snell's MATH results are for PaLM 2-S* with a PRM; Shojaee's puzzle regimes are on synthetic puzzles, so the two halves of the claim are different settings.

claim: Where a sound external check exists, most of the gain of an iterate-and-verify loop comes from the check, not from the critique text or from tree structure. GPT-4: Game of 24 5% to 36-38%, Blocksworld 40% to 83-87%, with critique-free sampling (k=25) reaching 42% on Game of 24. Coverage on SWE-bench Lite rose from 15.9% to 56% with 250 samples because unit tests could pick the winner.
agent_test: Ablate critique text with the code check kept. Expect little loss.
audit_note: Minor: Blocksworld 83-87% is the F.E.F/A.E.F critique variants; binary-feedback only gets 60% and critique-free k=25 sampling gets 72%, so critique content adds some gain there, but most still comes from the check. Both sources are from different labs (Kambhampati group vs Stanford/Brown).

claim: The quality of the scorer bounds the gain from search. A model-based value function loses correct branches and, with deeper search, is over-exploited. Self-consistency on the scorer (n=20) added 8.5 points in web-agent search.
agent_test: Measure pruned-correct rate with a held-out check. Compare model scorer, model scorer with self-consistency, and code check at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models fail by fixating on an early wrong answer, and handing them the exact algorithm does not remove the collapse at high complexity (Tower of Hanoi, Checker Jumping). Others have criticised the setup (token limits, unsolvable instances); those critiques were not opened.
agent_test: Test a forced-alternative step after the first committed answer on a collapse-size puzzle set, with a code executor for exact steps.

claim: Models satisfy single constraints far more often than all constraints together. TravelPlanner, GPT-4-Turbo test set: commonsense pass 63.3% per item but 2.0% per plan; hard-constraint pass 10.5% per item and 5.5% per plan; final pass 0.6%.
agent_test: Add a code-checked constraint ledger to a TravelPlanner subset and compare final pass rate at equal tokens.

claim: Samples from different models are not independent branches. Pairwise similarity across models is 71 to 82%, so sibling-model ensembles give less diversity than expected.
agent_test: Compare branches from one model forced into different solution families with branches from several models; measure embedding distance and verified quality.

claim: Tree search with a budget can help on open-ended, long-horizon tasks when the final outcome is exactly checkable, and the gain scales with search depth and breadth together (24.5% at d=1,b=1 up to 37.0% on 200 VWA tasks).
agent_test: Re-run with depth and breadth varied independently at equal total calls to find which carries the gain (Gap 3).
